questions.q: What is the industry-wide default order for customizing model behavior?
options: Fine-tuning first, prompting only if that fails
Prompting and retrieval first, fine-tuning only if those aren't enough
Retrieval only — fine-tuning and prompting are both discouraged
There is no agreed-upon order; it's purely a coin flip
questions.explain: Prompting and retrieval are cheap, fast, and reversible; fine-tuning is the costlier, slower option reserved for when those genuinely aren't enough.

questions.q: Which problem is generally best solved with retrieval (RAG) rather than fine-tuning?
options: The model doesn't know a specific recent fact
The model needs to consistently follow a narrow, hard-to-describe style
A long repeated system prompt is costing too many tokens per call
The model needs specialized jargon baked into its default behavior
questions.explain: Teaching new facts is retrieval's job — fine-tuning is an expensive, unreliable way to inject facts and tends to memorize examples rather than generalize.

questions.q: As of late 2026, what is the state of Anthropic's own Claude API with respect to fine-tuning?
options: It has no self-serve fine-tuning endpoint — Bedrock or professional services only
It offers full self-serve fine-tuning identical to OpenAI's
It only supports fine-tuning for enterprise customers via a web dashboard
It deprecated fine-tuning for all providers industry-wide
questions.explain: Anthropic's documented customization path is prompting/context-based; actual fine-tuning of Claude models runs through Amazon Bedrock or professional services, not a self-serve Claude API call.

questions.q: What is happening to OpenAI's self-serve fine-tuning API as of late 2026?
options: It's being expanded to support many more base models
It's being wound down, with new job creation ending in January 2027
It's becoming free for all users
Nothing has changed about its availability
questions.explain: OpenAI has blocked new organizations from fine-tuning since mid-2026 and has stated that new fine-tuning job creation ends in January 2027.

questions.q: In the lesson's decision framework, what should you check first?
options: Whether you have hundreds of training examples
Whether the base model is about to be deprecated
Whether a better prompt or retrieval can fix the problem
Whether your budget allows for training compute
questions.explain: The framework starts by asking whether prompting or retrieval resolves the issue — only when that's insufficient do the other questions matter.
